explanation: In France, a thumbs-up is a well-understood, positive sign of approval or 'good job,' the same as in most of North America and Western Europe. It's fine in casual and most everyday contexts, though a verbal response is more natural in very formal settings.
local_tip: Use it freely with friends, service staff, or colleagues to show approval; in formal business settings, pair it with (or replace it with) a verbal acknowledgment.

also_check.note: The thumbs-up is widely considered an offensive, dismissive insult, roughly equivalent to the middle finger.
The thumbs-up is traditionally seen as a vulgar gesture, similar in effect to showing the middle finger.
In some parts of Nigeria and West Africa, a thumbs-up can be read as rude or dismissive rather than purely positive.

sources.title: The Common Gesture You Should Never Make At A French Restaurant
